name: Senegal

findings.controller: Agence de l'Informatique de l'Etat (ADIE), Senegal's state IT agency
findings.financier: China Eximbank (per AidData; DCD says only 'a Chinese loan')
findings.summary: Senegal's national Tier-3 data centre in the Diamniadio technology park, built with Huawei equipment on a Chinese loan, was commissioned in June 2021; the president ordered all state data and platforms migrated to it.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary) Chinese Development Finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Building is state-owned and operated, so pole is domestic; Huawei (builder/equipment) and China Exim (financier) do not set the pole under SPEC v0.2. Huawei-supplied IT equipment inside is captured in SEN-002 bundle. DCD's 46bn CFA figure converts to roughly US$80m, not the US$18.2m it states, so value left null. Georgetown commentary instead ties the data centre to an earlier US$85m Exim broadband loan (2016); attribution between the two loans unresolved. ADIE has since been reorganised (Sénégal Numérique SA reported); current operation not confirmed in this pass.

findings.summary: Smart Senegal Phase 1, a China Exim concessional loan (RMB 1.05bn) contracted to Huawei, delivered a submarine cable landing, public WiFi, school networks, citizen service centres and the Diamniadio data-centre hub, completed June 2021.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary) Chinese Development Finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: AidData records the project as completed; Georgetown commentary (S4) describes the same components. Only one opened S1-S3 source, so uncorroborated. Coded under networks as the dominant component; equipment vendor Huawei sets the pole. RMB 1.05bn not converted (AidData's constant-2023 figure of about US$160m is a deflated estimate, not an announced value).

findings.local_actor: ADIE with the Defence and Security Forces
findings.summary: Senegal's Safe City programme, a Huawei-contracted component of Smart Senegal, installed roughly 500 surveillance cameras with command centres across Dakar, Thiès, Touba, Saint-Louis, Kaolack and other cities.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary) Chinese Development Finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: CIO Mag (March 2020) confirms 473 of 500 planned cameras installed by ADIE but does not name the vendor; Huawei as contractor rests on AidData alone, so the controller attribution is uncorroborated. Georgetown commentary alleges facial-recognition use against opposition members 2021-2024; that is the author's claim, not verified here. Audit 2026-10-28: CIO Mag names no camera vendor; AidData names Huawei for Smart Senegal but gives no camera count, so the Huawei-camera link is an inference; cameras largely in by March 2020; Georgetown says 13 cities.

findings.summary: Huawei built Senegal's government intranet in successive phases from 2006 (E-gov 1 and 2, about 3,000 km of fibre), extended by a national broadband project financed by a US$85m China Exim loan launched in 2016.
findings.analyst_inference: Single S4 commentary source; values (US$49.6m, US$100m, US$85m) come from that author and were not verified, so left null. Pre-2016 phases are pre-2020; current use of Huawei equipment in the state backbone not confirmed (still_current null). Audit 2026-10-28: Georgetown page dated 2025-10-20.

findings.summary: Sonatel partnered with Huawei for its 5G trials, including a live test in Dakar in November 2020 and the Orange 5G Lab opened in Dakar in 2022 with Huawei as main partner.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded tier 2 (pilot/trial partnership): Sonatel launched commercial 5G on 1 June 2024 after a CFA34.5bn licence, but no source opened names the vendor of its commercial RAN or core, so Huawei supplying the live 5G network is plausible but unconfirmed. Ecofin is cited for the commercial launch context only.

findings.local_actor: Tigo Senegal (later Free, now Yas / Axian)
findings.summary: Tigo Senegal chose Ericsson as preferred supplier for a three-year modernisation of more than 1,000 sites, covering radio (2G-4G, IoT), microwave backhaul, cloud packet core, OSS and transport.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson is Swedish, so pole third. Pre-2020 and the operator has since changed hands and rebranded (Free, then Yas under Axian); whether Ericsson remains the RAN/core vendor was not confirmed. The source does not say whether a previous vendor was replaced. Rebrand chain is background knowledge, not stated in the source.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Communication, Telecommunications and Digital Economy
findings.summary: Senegal's digital ministry signed a memorandum of understanding with Google to create a sovereign cloud keeping critical government and business data in local infrastructure, plus cloud skills training.
findings.analyst_inference: Neither source says who would own or operate the sovereign cloud or whether Google technology (e.g. a distributed/air-gapped offering) would run it; coded us on the assumption Google supplies the platform. If the state operates it on its own hardware the pole could become domestic. No implementation evidence found as of October 2026.

findings.builder: Snef, SERTEM Groupe, Kent Data Centres
findings.summary: Axian's data-centre arm Stellarix is expanding its Senegal facility to meet AI demand, with French engineering firm Snef among contributors; capacity, site and investment were not disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 4 because the source describes the expansion as underway, but no construction milestone is documented; could be tier 2-3. Axian is headquartered in Madagascar, so pole third. Single source. Audit 2026-10-28: Neither Billionaires.Africa nor TechAfrica News reports a construction milestone; tier 4 -> 2 (announced expansion).

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Communication, Telecommunications and Digital Economy (New Deal Technologique)
findings.summary: Senegal unveiled a planned 'Senegal AI Factory', a national compute and applied-research infrastructure under its New Deal Technologique, at a Tokyo event; funding, partners and GPU supplier remain undetermined.
findings.analyst_inference: Stated intent only; the source mentions possible Japanese, European or Gulf partners without naming any. Pole domestic as a planned state facility; controller will depend on financing and hardware choices.

silicon.null_reason: AI-data-centre and Senegal AI Factory searches surfaced no accelerator purchases, GPU vendor or export licence; the AI Factory source says the GPU supplier is undecided

models.null_reason: one search on national AI partnerships found a UNDP accord and a Sénégal Numérique-GalsenAI tie-up (snippets only) but no frontier-model provider partnership or sovereign Senegalese model

power.null_reason: no AI-specific power evidence surfaced; Axian's NEA Kolda solar plant was mentioned alongside the data-centre business but not documented as dedicated supply

corrections.note: Source-verified corrections and audit notes: SEN-003, SEN-004, SEN-008
